title: Selvatico Estense to Giuseppe Riva, Paris, Oct 1719 (not in the catalogue): the 2 Oct letter read in part from its interlinear gloss, the 27 Oct letter decoded with the frozen key, not read; the 1722 letters of lead 1568 not solved

plaintext.source: Contemporary interlinear decipherment over the cipher, legible in part (about 60%). A transcription job: ff. 4r-5r gave the key, ff. 5v-6v were held out.

system.summary: Numbers: vowels 1-5, consonants 6-15, syllables 21-24 (la le li lo), 25 r, 26 s, 27 t, 29 z, second homophones 31 a, 34 o, 35 v; underlined small numbers are short words (3_ in, 4_ il, 7_ con, 8_ e); numbers above about 40 are code words. A curl written before many groups is not a sign.
system.notes: Underline marks short words on small numbers; superscript letters (^a, ^e, ^Cno) mark endings and are not interpreted by the frozen key. Some groups are written run together with dots (8.4.3); they are split into groups. The 1722 letters use another table (groups mostly 50-95, heavy underlining).

prior_solution.where: The 2 Oct letter carries its own contemporary interlinear decipherment (legible in part). No edition or modern decipherment of these letters found: Dan's catalogue, leads and Dudout list (1568 is the Riva lead, the 1722 letters; the 1719 letters are not listed), three web searches; Lindgren and Timms print Riva's Steffani letters, not these (3 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (lead 1568 and the neighbouring Estense items) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, built and froze the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (decryption, mark check, held-out test, 1722 tests)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: Eight Selvatico letters fetched from the Estense IIIF service as tiles, one request at a time.
Catalogue, leads, Dudout list and two web searches: no edition or decipherment.
Two sign passes of both 1719 letters from full-size crops (pass A blind to the gloss); 704 of 1024 groups agree.
Key built from the interlinear gloss pairs of ff. 4r-5r only, frozen before testing (key_frozen.tsv).
Held-out ff. 5v-6v against the gloss, first by hand (about 31 of 40); later scripted (see below).
27 Oct letter decrypted with the frozen key and read where it gives sense: phrases on the Tuscan succession, Lorraine, Monferrato, Mademoiselle de Valois; much stays fragmentary.
1719 key and shifts by 30, 50, 60 tried on the 1722 letters: 33% of groups covered as letters, no words.
Ciphertext-only homophonic attack on the 1722 letters with Italian quadgrams, two runs, not tuned.

Independent blind check (VERIFY.md): 188 groups of 5v-6r, 9 value-changing differences (4.8%); solver wrong on 4 + 1 probable; parser hole found (18 tokens dropped, one unmarked omission of Re); Cyrillic letter in a reading; local paths in scripts.

Five groups corrected on crops (5v.L11, 6r.L02, 6r.L09, 6r.L10, 6r.L15); parser splits run-together groups and flags any unparsable token; check_marks lets only a bracket absorb them; three reading lines corrected.

Held-out test scripted against a corrected gloss file: 44 of 63 gloss words exact with the frozen key; of 56 with no uncovered code group, 44 exact, 7 need only a post-test value, 4 differ in a marked ending, 1 miss. No letter value contradicted.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key built from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of ff. 4r-5r of the 2 Oct letter, frozen, then tested on the held-out ff. 5v-6v against the same gloss and applied unchanged to the 27 Oct letter.
outcome.fraction_read_source: check_marks.py: 159 words with no mark in the 2 Oct cipher passages, over 439 cipher-passage words of both 1719 letters; the 27 Oct letter (190 tokens, 116 unmarked, many fragments) is counted as not read. The 1722 letters are not in this denominator.

texts.label: 2 Oct 1719, cc. 4-7
texts.summary: On the peace congress and the succession of Tuscany against Lorraine; Orléans, as brother-in-law of Lorraine, would need a stronger tie with Modena, the marriage with Mademoiselle de Valois; Count Scotti's appointment out of proportion to his birth; the Regent's daughter; Lord Stair; jealousy; the common master.
texts.note: Words in the cipher passages 249: 159 with no mark (64%); 4r-5r 88 of 136 (the key was built from this gloss), held-out 5v-6v 71 of 113. Holes in place for code numbers and post-test values.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Coherent sense across 4r-5r (built from the gloss, so circular as key evidence) and on the held-out pages 6r-6v: the Tuscany succession, Lorraine, Orléans, the Valois marriage, Scotti's appointment out of proportion to his birth, the daughter of the Regent, Stair, jealousy, the common master. Weak places: 4r.L10 [0_] efic[33]; 4v.L10-13 [160], a[...]; 5r.L01-06 [91] [170] [200] [78] [16_]; 5v.L12-15 [fisi], [sip33], [?] figura, [57]; 6r.L10, where Re was omitted with no mark (since corrected); 6v.L04-05 [264], [126], [60_]; 6v.L09 [52] [208].

texts.label: 27 Oct 1719, cc. 12-13
texts.summary: Fragments only: the succession of Tuscany, Lorraine excluded, Monferrato, 'in mancanza delle linee viventi', Mademoiselle de Valois, 'seminar confusione'. 'Queen mother' and 'Duchess of Berry' are conjectures.
texts.note: 190 tokens, 116 without a mark (61%), but many unmarked tokens are fragments ('d', 'far', 'li le e se-'); the independent reviewer estimates about 50% reads as sense and graded the reading C. Decoded with the frozen key, not read.
